Nothing in the record ties the driven segment to that road: F3 carries only km and distance from the route, and the driver's own statement says he went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead because it "looked clearer" [F11]. ✓ ruling consistent with the policy certificate

certificate: ✓ RD-1 off-route segment(s) exist [case] 1 segment(s) (F3)
✗ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F3] no qualifying incident (speed band alone does not exempt) (no evidence)

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 23:03:00 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 22:59 driver: “Jam on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Upper Paya Lebar Road?”; F9: Chat #2 23:00 rider: “Sure, no problem.”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I asked the rider about going via Upper Paya Lebar Road and the rider agreed. In the end I went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead because it looked clearer; same direction.” (F8, F9, F11)

RD-3 rider-requested stop; whether the rider named this place [F3] RULE (RD-3(a)): exempt if a RIDER message before the segment named a specific place and the car stopped there (the whole way there is exempt; how long the stop lasted or how far the place was does not reduce it). A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. No stop measured in this segment. (F8, F9)
